name: Cerro de los Ángeles
story: The hill at Getafe, near Spain's geographic centre, carried the monument to the Sacred Heart of Jesus consecrated by Alfonso XIII in 1919. In the anticlerical violence of summer 1936, militiamen staged a mock 'execution' of the statue by firing squad, photographed for the press, and the monument was dynamited on 7 August. In November the Nationalists took the hill and it remained close to the front for the rest of the war. Franco's regime rebuilt a larger monument (1944–1965), a symbol of the 'crusade' narrative.
see: The rebuilt monument and basilica; ruins of the original monument and bullet marks on the monument and convent walls.
plan: Free; open daily. Drive or bus from Getafe; views over southern Madrid.
